headline: Law funds most of the Department of Homeland Security for 2026, excluding ICE and Border Patrol, and ends a partial shutdown with back pay.
what_it_does: This law provides full-year 2026 funding for most Homeland Security agencies, including TSA, the Coast Guard, FEMA, the Secret Service, USCIS, and cybersecurity programs, but not ICE or the Border Patrol. It covers the partial Homeland Security shutdown that began February 14, 2026, and requires back pay for affected federal workers. It also sets many rules on how the money can be spent, such as limits on detention practices, new reporting duties, and deadlines for FEMA disaster payments.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees affected by the shutdown
who_it_affects.how: They are to receive back pay for the time their agency's funding lapsed.

who_it_affects.group: Pregnant women in Homeland Security custody
who_it_affects.how: The law limits the use of restraints on them and requires health and safety standards for pregnant and postpartum people in border custody.

who_it_affects.group: People held in Homeland Security custody
who_it_affects.how: Records about deaths, abuse, or alleged misconduct in custody may not be destroyed, and some of these records must be made available to people punished based on them.

who_it_affects.group: Communities and people seeking disaster aid
who_it_affects.how: FEMA must post a public dashboard tracking reimbursement requests, and agency leadership funding is cut each day too many requests sit in final review for more than 60 days.

who_it_affects.group: Air travelers, including members of Congress
who_it_affects.how: TSA may not exempt members of Congress and certain federal officials from standard passenger and baggage screening.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy prescription drugs from Canada
who_it_affects.how: Customs and Border Protection may not use this money to stop individuals from bringing in personal-use amounts of certain prescription drugs from Canada.
Homeland Security may not collect new border crossing fees or study adding one.

who_it_affects.group: Journalists and people facing criminal charges
who_it_affects.how: The department's intelligence office may not target journalists doing their jobs or interview people with pending criminal cases without their consent after talking to a lawyer.
The law provides money for a pay raise for them in 2026.
FEMA may waive certain matching and other requirements for firefighter staffing and equipment grants.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Congress and their staff
who_it_affects.how: Homeland Security may not block them from entering immigration detention facilities for oversight visits or change facilities temporarily to alter what they see.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 30, 2026; funding covers fiscal year 2026, and shutdown-related provisions reach back to February 14, 2026.
